planting.note: Divide and replant rooted cuttings in spring after frost danger passes.

directions: A large bronze spider-type exhibition mum bred by Ted King and named to commemorate a National Chrysanthemum Society show held at Descanso Gardens in Southern California. Blooms open late in the season, from late October into mid-November, carried squarely on strong, upright stems. For maximum show-sized blooms, disbud each stem to a single terminal flower rather than letting the plant branch into sprays.

planting.note: Divide and replant rooted cuttings in spring after frost danger passes.

directions: A large exhibition spider mum bred by Ted King from a Japanese seedling parent, producing light pink florets that fade toward a contrasting white center. Blooms arrive from mid-October into early November on stems of medium height. Growers aiming for exhibition size should disbud to one terminal bloom per stem; left natural it can also be grown in spray form.

planting.note: Divide and replant rooted cuttings in spring after frost danger passes.

directions: A tall, large-flowered spider mum in deep orchid-purple, blooming from late October into early November. Its narrow, slightly hooked florets open gradually over several weeks and are carried on notably strong, upright stems. Disbud for exhibition-size single blooms, or allow the plant to branch for a spray of smaller flowers.

planting.note: Divide and replant rooted cuttings in spring after frost danger passes.

directions: A tall exhibition spider mum blending coral, orange, and gold tones in a single bloom, set off by dark green foliage. Flowering runs mid-to-late October, and the sturdy stems hold blooms upright without staking. Disbud to one terminal flower per stem for the largest, most fully colored show blooms.

planting.note: Divide and replant rooted cuttings in spring after frost danger passes.

directions: A tall spider-type exhibition mum with dusty mauve florets tipped in burgundy, giving blooms a creamy, two-toned cup shape from a distance. Flowering runs from mid-October into early November on long, tubular petals typical of the spider class. Grow as a disbudded single stem for the best exhibition form.

planting.note: Divide and replant rooted cuttings in spring after frost danger passes.

directions: One of the earlier-blooming spider mums, opening buff-yellow florets with lightly curled, light-red tips from mid-October. The medium-height habit suits both garden beds and large containers better than taller spider cultivars. Disbud for exhibition-size single blooms, or leave natural for a fuller display of smaller flowers.

planting.note: Divide and replant rooted cuttings in spring after frost danger passes.

directions: A pink spider mum with long, fine florets, named for a granddaughter of Ray and Kim Gray, the current owners of King's Mums. It has an unusually long bloom window, opening flowers from mid-October clear through mid-November. Disbud for a single large exhibition bloom per stem, or let it branch naturally to produce abundant lateral stems for cutting.

planting.note: Divide and replant rooted cuttings in spring after frost danger passes.

directions: A deep yellow exhibition spider mum named for the hometown of growers Ray and Kim Gray, with bloom form often compared to the well-known 'Golden Splendor'. It is among the earliest spider cultivars to flower, starting in early October and continuing into November. Disbud for show-quality single blooms, though it also performs well grown as cut-flower sprays.

planting.note: Divide and replant rooted cuttings in spring after frost danger passes.

directions: A deep golden-brown spider mum whose blooms are laced with hundreds of fine, threadlike florets arranged in symmetrical, radiating fullness. It flowers from mid-to-late October and holds its form for an extended period once open. Disbud for the fullest exhibition-size flower; the plant's symmetry makes it a favorite for show tables.

planting.note: Divide and replant rooted cuttings in spring after frost danger passes.

directions: A tall spider mum in deep purple with crimson-tipped florets that stand out stiffly, giving the bloom a starburst appearance often described as nearly fluorescent in color. It flowers from late October into early November. Disbud to a single terminal bloom per stem to show off its distinctive structure and color contrast at full size.
